claims: A major, high-impact winter storm is forecast to bring heavy snow, high winds, and blizzard conditions to parts of the Midwest and Northern Plains on March 14-15, 2026.
Dangerous travel conditions are expected in parts of the Midwest and Northern Plains on March 14-15, 2026.
The Southwest will experience a summer-like heat dome with temperatures exceeding 100°F.
Heavy snow develops Saturday evening through Sunday in Midwest/Upper Midwest (MN, SD, WI).
Over 10-15 inches of snow is possible in some areas of Midwest/Upper Midwest (MN, SD, WI).
A strong cold front will bring rain to the Eastern US.
Potential frost/freeze conditions exist early next week in the Eastern US.
Record-breaking early-season heat is forecast for the Southwest US.
Highs surpassing 100°F are forecast for the Southwest US.
A threat of severe thunderstorms exists on Sunday in the Gulf Coast/South.
Potential damaging winds exist on Sunday in the Gulf Coast/South.
Cold weather moves eastward behind the weekend storm early next week.
